questions.q: What is a cascading parameter setup?
options: A parameter that automatically refreshes every five minutes
A way to hide a parameter from the report viewer toolbar
A single checkbox that makes one parameter accept multiple values
A chain of parameters where each one's available values depend on the value chosen for the parameter before it
questions.explain: Cascading parameters chain together — picking a category narrows the subcategory list, picking a subcategory narrows the product list, and so on.

questions.q: In a Category → Subcategory → Product cascade, how many datasets are typically needed just to supply available values?
options: One — a single dataset can supply values for all three parameters
Three — one per parameter level, each filtered by the parameter above it
Two — Category and Product only, Subcategory is automatic
Zero — cascading parameters don't use datasets at all
questions.explain: Each level needs its own dataset: an independent Category dataset, a Subcategory dataset filtered by @Category, and a Product dataset filtered by @Subcategory.

questions.q: Why must Category come before Subcategory in the Report Data pane's Parameters node?
options: The order only affects cosmetic layout, not functionality
Report Builder assigns order randomly and it cannot be changed
Because the Subcategory dataset's query references @Category, which must already have a chosen value
Alphabetical order is required for all report parameters
questions.explain: Parameter order in the Report Data pane determines the order a reader is prompted — and a parameter can't reference a value that hasn't been chosen yet.

questions.q: What does the Subcategory dataset's query typically include that the Category dataset's query does not?
options: A hardcoded list of every possible subcategory
A reference to the report's title
A join to the Report Server's configuration database
A reference to @Category in its WHERE clause, filtering subcategories to the chosen category
questions.explain: The Subcategory dataset's query filters using @Category (e.g., WHERE CategoryID = @Category) so it only returns subcategories belonging to the chosen category.

questions.q: What does the report's main dataset (the one driving the table or matrix) usually reference?
options: All of the cascading parameters in the chain, so the final report reflects every choice made
Only the last parameter in the chain
None of the parameters — the main dataset ignores parameter values entirely
Only the first parameter in the chain
questions.explain: The main report dataset typically references Category, Subcategory, and Product together in its WHERE clause so the displayed data reflects the reader's full set of choices.
